art.subject: Common Swift (Apus apus), adult of the eastern race pekinensis, in late spring: dark sooty brown, a little paler and browner than western birds, with a paler forehead and a clear whitish throat patch that is larger in this race; wings blackish brown, the inner flight feathers slightly paler in good light; rump dark, the same colour as the back; underparts dark brown, uniform at a distance, with only faint, narrow pale fringes visible close up. Tiny black bill; dark eye; tiny feathered feet hidden in flight.
art.pose: in fast flight high over a ridge, wings swept back like a sickle, seen from slightly below
art.scene: Korean coastal hills under a wide late-spring sky in May; no people, buildings or text
views: adult in flight seen squarely from below: head, body and tail in one line, scythe-shaped wings spread straight out to the sides to their full span, swept back from the wrist close to the body, sharply demarcated pale whitish throat patch, pale forehead, uniformly dark brown body, slightly paler inner flight feathers, forked tail, feet hidden

adult in flight seen squarely from above: head, body and tail in one line, scythe-shaped dark brown wings spread straight out to the sides to their full span, bent back at the wrist close to the body, slightly paler secondaries and inner primaries, dark brown back and rump with no white band, forked tail
art.build: Swift a little larger than a Barn Swallow but with much longer wings; about the size of the Pacific Swift, with a shorter, less deeply forked tail. Slim, torpedo-shaped body, short broad head with no visible neck, tiny bill with a wide gape. Wings very long, narrow and scythe-shaped, swept back from a short arm. Tail of medium length with a shallow fork, often closed to a point. Legs tiny and almost never seen; it never perches on wires or twigs. Flight fast, with flickering wingbeats and long glides.
avoid: Do not paint a white rump band or bold whitish scaling on the underparts; these mark the Pacific Swift (Apus pacificus), the common swift in Korea.
Do not paint it like a swallow: no white or orange underparts, no long tail streamers, no perching on a wire.
Do not give it a deeply forked tail; the fork is shallow.
Do not show visible legs or a large bill.
